features.name: Media library scanning and updating
steps: Add several video and audio files to the device
Launch VLC
Grant media access permission
Automatically scan the media library
Videos appear on the "videos" page and audio on the "audio" page
Then add or delete files in the scanned directory
Re-enter/refresh
The media library content changes in sync.
features.expected: After granting media permission the scan must complete automatically; videos and audio appear on their respective category pages with counts matching the real files; after adding or deleting files a media-library refresh must change in sync; the scan results must persist and not be lost after restarting the app.

features.name: Video media-library browsing and playback
steps: Prepare several videos
Enter "videos"
Show the video cover, title, and media information
Tap any video
Open the player and start playback
Return to the media library
Then open another video
The playback content switches correctly.
features.expected: The list must show the cover, title, and media information; tapping a video must genuinely open the player and play that video; after returning to the media library the list state is preserved; opening another video must switch the playback content.

features.name: Video search
steps: The video library contains several media with different names
Tap search
Enter a title keyword
The list keeps only matching media
Changing the search term changes the results in real time
Clear the search
The full media list is restored.
features.expected: The results must be filtered by keyword keeping only matching media; changing the search term changes the results in real time; clearing restores the full list; no match shows an empty state; searching must not delete or modify media data.

features.name: Media library sorting
steps: Prepare media with different names, artists, durations, and time attributes
Open the display settings
Select "name / artist name / length / release time / insertion time" respectively
Switch between ascending and descending
Verify that the media arrangement order genuinely changes.
features.expected: Each sort mode must genuinely change the list order with ascending and descending giving opposite results; the sort state must persist, and after leaving the page and returning it still sorts by the selected mode; merely changing the UI text is not enough.

features.name: List display and favorites filtering
steps: Switch to "display as list" in the media library
The layout switches from cards/grid to list
Mark some media as favorites
Enable "show favorites only"
Non-favorite media is hidden
The full content is restored after disabling.
features.expected: The list and grid layouts must genuinely switch while keeping the same media set; with show-favorites-only enabled non-favorite media is hidden but its data is not deleted; disabling it restores everything; the favorite state persists.

features.name: Audio category browsing
steps: Import audio with different artist, album, track, and genre metadata
Open "audio"
Switch between "artists / albums / tracks / genres / playlists"
Each page reorganizes the songs according to the corresponding metadata
Tap the song to start playback.
features.expected: The artists, albums, tracks, genres, and playlists pages must group by real metadata, with the same song pointing to the same media in different categories; after switching categories the list content changes accordingly; tapping a song enters playback.

features.name: Local file browsing
steps: Enter "browse"
Open internal storage
Enter folders level by level
Locate the video or audio file
Tapping a file plays it directly
The previous directory position is still preserved after returning
Other directories can continue to be entered.
features.expected: The directory hierarchy must reflect the real file system; tapping a media file plays it directly; after returning the previous directory position is preserved; an empty directory should show an empty state rather than an error.

features.name: Favorites for frequently used folders
steps: Find Download, Movies, Music, or other directories under "browse"
Add the directory to favorites
Return to the browse home
The corresponding folder appears in the favorites area
Tapping a favorite jumps directly to the original directory
The card disappears after removing the favorite.
features.expected: A favorited directory must appear in the favorites area of the browse home and be able to jump directly to the original directory; after removal the card disappears; the favorite relationship must persist across restarts; an ordinary file must not be favorited as a folder.

features.name: Local network browsing
steps: Open "browse network"
Show the server when an accessible LAN media source exists
Enter the server
Browse the remote directory
Select media
Play directly in VLC
Return to the network browsing page and continue accessing other files.
features.expected: When an accessible LAN media source exists the server must be listed; after entering, the real remote directory can be browsed and remote media played; when no server is available an empty state should be shown rather than crashing.

features.name: Playlist creation and management
steps: Choose "add to playlist" from the media item menu
Create or choose a playlist
Several videos enter the same playlist
Open the "playlists" page
Show the name, cover, track count, and total duration
Tap to start sequential playback.
features.expected: The playlist must persist; the name, cover, track count, and total duration match the media actually added; tapping play follows the list order; deleting a playlist does not affect the original media files.

features.name: Shuffle playback of a playlist
steps: Prepare a playlist containing at least 3 media items
Open the playlist menu
Choose "shuffle"
Start playback
The subsequent media order differs from the original list order
After stopping and re-entering the whole list still plays normally.
features.expected: In shuffle mode the playback order must not be exactly the list order; the queue should cover the media in the list without duplication or omission; after stopping, replaying the whole list still works normally.

features.name: Media queue operations
steps: Open the menu on a media item
Test "add to playback queue" and "insert as next item" respectively
Open the current playback queue
Normally added media goes to the back of the queue, while media "inserted as next item" goes right after the current media
After the current playback ends it plays in the new queue order.
features.expected: Media added to the playback queue goes to the back, while media inserted as next item goes right after the current media; after the current playback ends it plays in the new queue order; queue changes should be immediately visible.

features.name: Play the video as audio
steps: Choose "play as audio" on a video item
It does not enter the normal full-screen video playback UI, and the video picture is not the main output
The audio track keeps playing
It can be paused, resumed, and seeked
The audio playback state is preserved after returning to the media library.
features.expected: After selecting, it must not enter the normal full-screen video playback UI; the audio track must keep playing and can be paused, resumed, and seeked; the audio playback state is preserved after returning to the media library.

features.name: Media favorites, renaming, and deletion
steps: Open the item menu on a media item
Add to favorites
The favorite state changes
Perform the renaming
The name in the media library updates in sync
Perform the deletion
The file disappears from the media library and does not reappear after rescanning.
features.expected: The favorite state must persist; after renaming the media-library name updates in sync; after deletion the file disappears from the media library and does not reappear after rescanning; a cancelled operation must not modify the file.

features.name: Play history
steps: First play several different videos/audio files
Enter "more
History"
History records appear in playback order
Tapping a history item replays it
Continue playing new media after disabling the "play history" setting
New media no longer enters the history.
features.expected: History records appear in playback order and persist; tapping a history item replays it; after disabling play history new plays no longer enter the records, but existing records should not be cleared without reason.

features.name: Network streaming playback
steps: Enter "more
streaming"
Enter a valid http://, mms://, or rtsp:// media address
Submit
VLC attempts to establish a connection
After success it enters the player
Normal playback operations such as pause and dragging the progress are available.
features.expected: After submitting a valid address it must attempt to connect and enter the player; normal playback operations such as pause and dragging the progress are available; an invalid address must give an error response rather than no response.

features.name: Basic video playback controls
steps: Open the video
The player shows the current time, total duration, and progress bar
Tap play/pause
The state switches correctly
Tap previous/next
Jump within the playback queue
Drag the progress bar
The playback position moves to the target time.
features.expected: The time display advances with playback and matches the total duration; play and pause must genuinely switch the audio state; previous and next switch the media in the queue; after dragging the progress bar the playback position matches the displayed time.

features.name: Gestures control the playback progress, volume, and brightness
steps: Play the video
Swipe left/right in the gesture-enabled area
Rewind/fast-forward the playback position
Swipe up/down in the corresponding area
Adjust the volume or screen brightness
The new value takes effect after releasing
Subsequent playback continues from the current position.
features.expected: Swiping left/right must change the playback position, with the rewind/fast-forward direction matching the swipe; swiping up/down adjusts the volume and brightness respectively; after releasing, the new values take effect and remain for subsequent playback.

features.name: Double-tap and multi-touch player operations
steps: Enable the corresponding control setting
Double-tap the center of the screen
Play/pause toggle
Double-tap the left/right edges of the screen
Rewind or fast-forward by the configured time
Pinch zoom
The video display scale changes
Playback continues after the gesture ends.
features.expected: Double-tapping the center toggles play and pause; double-tapping the left/right edges rewinds or fast-forwards by the configured time; pinching must change the video display scale; after the gesture ends playback continues without the picture jumping.

features.name: Playback speed and jump time
steps: Open the more menu during video playback
Choose "playback speed"
Adjust to a non-1.0× value
The video and audio playback speed change in sync
Then choose "go to time"
Enter the target time
The playhead jumps directly to the corresponding position.
features.expected: After changing the playback speed the audio and video change speed in sync and the UI must show the current speed value; after a go-to-time jump the playback position matches the input time; input exceeding the total duration should be limited.

features.name: Loop, shuffle, and A-B loop
steps: Play the video
Enable loop mode
After the media ends it replays according to the loop rule
After enabling shuffle the queue playback order changes
Enter A-B loop
Set start point A and end point B
The playback position loops only within the A/B interval
Normal playback is restored after cancelling.
features.expected: In loop mode the media replays according to the rule after ending; shuffle changes the queue order; during A-B loop the playback position can only loop within the A/B interval and returns to normal after cancelling; point A must be earlier than point B.

features.name: Sleep timer
steps: Play a video or audio
Open the more menu
Enter the "sleep timer"
Set an end time/delay
Playback continues
Playback stops automatically according to the setting when the time arrives
The timer state updates according to the UI logic when playback restarts.
features.expected: Playback must stop automatically when the set time arrives; reopening the timer should reflect the current remaining-time state; after cancelling it no longer stops automatically; playback is unaffected while the setting is active.

features.name: Video bookmarks
steps: Play a long video
Jump to a certain time point
Open "bookmarks"
Add a bookmark at the current position
Continue playing to other positions
Reopen the bookmark list
Tap the previous bookmark
The playback position returns accurately to the saved time point.
features.expected: Bookmarks must record an accurate time point and persist; the list shows the corresponding time; after tapping a bookmark the playback position matches the saved time; different videos' bookmarks must not mix data.

features.name: Floating player / background playback
steps: During video playback choose "pop out player" or switch apps according to the "background/PiP mode" setting
The video shrinks to a floating playback window or enters the configured background mode
Media continues after switching to another app
Return to VLC
The normal player state and original playback progress are restored.
features.expected: After switching apps the media must continue playing without interruption or duplication; the player appears as a floating window; after returning to VLC it restores the normal player while keeping the original playback progress.

features.name: Player control settings and behavior linkage
steps: Enter the player's "control settings"

Modify the parameters shown in the screenshot such as audio boost, save audio delay, continue playing video, volume gestures, brightness gestures, remember brightness, swipe to seek, pinch zoom, double-tap to seek, double-tap play/pause, fast forward, locate button, fast-forward/rewind time, and control-bar auto-hide time
Return to the player
Perform the corresponding operations item by item
The player behavior must immediately change according to the new setting and persist across media where appropriate.
features.expected: Each setting must genuinely change the corresponding playback behavior, such as fast-forward/rewind time, gesture toggles, and control-bar auto-hide time; after disabling a gesture it no longer takes effect; the settings should persist across media.
